issues.description: GetLimit mutates a shared *RateLimit from the config map, racing across requests
issues.detail: rateLimit is the pointer stored in the descriptor tree (loadDescriptors set descriptor.limit = NewRateLimit(...)), and GetLimit hands it back to every caller. The new code does `rateLimit.Stats = this.statsManager.NewStats(enhancedKey)` and `rateLimit.FullKey = enhancedKey` on that shared pointer on every call, with a different key per runtime request. Concurrent requests will stomp Stats/FullKey on the same struct, and which key actually records the hit is a race. The existing detailed_metric branch had the same shape but at least produced a stable key per limit; value_to_metric makes the key request-dependent and turns the latent bug into a guaranteed one. The override must return a *copy* of RateLimit (or compute stats per-call without mutating the shared object), the way detailed_metric should have done in the first place.

issues.description: stats counters are created on every GetLimit call for every distinct runtime value
issues.detail: statsManager.NewStats(enhancedKey) is called inside GetLimit on the hot path, once per request, with a key that embeds runtime values like subject_id or route. That registers (and retains) a new stats struct in the underlying store for every unique value seen. detailed_metric has the same hazard and is documented as 'use with care'; value_to_metric inherits it but the README sells it as the safer alternative. At minimum the per-key stats need to be cached (look up first, create once) and the unbounded-cardinality risk needs to be in the docs in red, not buried in a 'NB' on the other feature.

issues.description: Dead `NewRateLimit` call immediately before overwriting Stats
issues.detail: The override block does `rateLimit = NewRateLimit(...rateLimit.FullKey...)` and then on the very next line `rateLimit.Stats = this.statsManager.NewStats(enhancedKey)` and `rateLimit.FullKey = enhancedKey`. The NewRateLimit call's only observable effect is the stats it just allocated, which are then thrown away. Either it's there to clone the struct (in which case do that explicitly and comment why) or it's noise. Right now it reads as cargo-culted and it allocates a stats entry under the *old* key for no reason — bad taste, and possibly contributing to cardinality.

issues.description: Two parallel key builders doing nearly the same work
issues.detail: GetLimit now maintains detailedMetricFullKey and valueToMetricFullKey side-by-side, each appending a per-level segment with overlapping logic (key vs key_value, wildcard handling, empty-value handling). The valueToMetric branch has three near-identical sub-blocks (wildcard / matchedUsingValue / default) that each end up doing 'write key, optionally write _value'. This is exactly the kind of special-casing the feature is supposed to be about: collapse it to one helper that returns the segment for a level given (entry, nextDescriptor, matchedViaWildcard, matchedUsingValue), and call it once. The diff would be half the size and the next maintainer wouldn't have to diff three branches against each other to convince themselves they agree.

issues.description: matchedUsingValue semantics are subtle and undocumented
issues.detail: `matchedUsingValue := nextDescriptor != nil` is set *before* the fallback to key-only lookup, then cleared if the fallback fires. After a wildcard match, matchedViaWildcard is true and matchedUsingValue is also true, and the code relies on checking wildcard first. This is correct but fragile, and there isn't a single comment explaining the state machine (wildcard / explicit key+value / default-key). Add a short comment or — better — make it an enum-ish local (matchKind) so the three downstream branches read as a switch instead of nested ifs.

issues.description: No test for the 'no descriptor matched' branch that still appends `entry.Key`
issues.detail: The else branch at the bottom of the per-entry block writes `entry.Key` into valueToMetricFullKey even when nextDescriptor is nil. Combined with the fact that the loop continues to the next entry, this produces a metric key that includes a segment for a descriptor that didn't actually match anything in the config. No test exercises this; whether it's intentional or a leftover from detailed_metric's shape is unclear. Either drop the segment when nextDescriptor is nil, or add a test and a comment explaining what key is expected.

issues.description: Positional struct literal for rateLimitDescriptor is now four fields and growing
issues.detail: `&rateLimitDescriptor{map[string]*rateLimitDescriptor{}, rateLimit, nil, descriptorConfig.ValueToMetric}` and `rateLimitDescriptor{map[string]*rateLimitDescriptor{}, nil, nil, false}` are positional. Adding the fourth field already required touching both call sites and getting the order right; the fifth will be a footgun. Use named-field initialization. Cheap fix, prevents a class of future bugs.

issues.description: Feature overlaps heavily with detailed_metric; consider whether it should exist
issues.detail: value_to_metric is, in effect, 'detailed_metric but only at the levels I tag, and ignored when detailed_metric wins'. That's a useful refinement, but the implementation is a parallel pipeline and the user-facing model is now two flags that interact via precedence. A cleaner shape would be a single per-descriptor enum (metric_value: none | key_only | key_and_value) or extending detailed_metric to take a per-level bool. Not a blocker, but worth pushing back on before the API surface freezes — two near-identical knobs are how config files become unmaintainable.

issues.description: Tests assert Stats.Key but not concurrent-safety; the real bug is invisible to them
issues.detail: All seven new tests are single-threaded and reuse a fresh rlConfig per scenario. The shared-pointer mutation in GetLimit will pass every one of them and fail in production under load. Add a test that calls GetLimit concurrently from N goroutines with different entry values against the same rlConfig and asserts each returned RateLimit's Stats.Key matches its own input. That test will currently fail, which is the point.

review.summary: The feature is useful and the user-facing model is reasonable, but the implementation has a real concurrency bug: GetLimit mutates the *RateLimit pointer that lives in the shared config tree, overwriting Stats and FullKey per request with a key derived from runtime values. Under concurrent load with different descriptor values this races. The detailed_metric branch had the same shape but with a stable key; value_to_metric turns it into a guaranteed bug. Separately, NewStats is being called per request per unique runtime value with no caching — the cardinality hazard the docs warn about for detailed_metric is now baked into value_to_metric and not mentioned. The key-building logic is also a three-way branch that wants to be one helper, and there's a dead NewRateLimit call inside the override block. NEEDS-WORK: fix the shared-state mutation (return a per-call copy, or compute and cache stats once per concrete key), collapse the parallel key builders, drop the dead allocation, and add a concurrent test before this lands.
